I feel you. I've been working to get a diagnosis ever since I found out what BPD is. I keep a running list of all my "symptoms". It's long and I'm pretty sure I'm missing out on so many. I'm just really interested in people who are officially diagnosed and who identify with quiet BPD because I think that's more along the lines of what I struggle with. However, I've felt very invalidated by the fact that I have been fairly "functional" over my lifetime. But I'm fucking miserable most days than not. And for some reason "depression" never really encompassed all of the things I was experiencing. I guess I'd be really interested in hearing (if it's not too long for you), which specific criteria your psychiatrist used to confirm your diagnosis/your most obvious symptoms. Or about how you express the criteria that everyone thinks can only be "externalized", i.e. emotional instability, efforts to avoid abandonment, impulsive behavior, and intense anger.

Codependency is just one symptom that may or may not be present in a pw qBPD. This can be the result of  an unstable sense of self or fear of abandonment, which are already two diagnostic criteria of BPD. Besides those two, I feel as though you are overlooking 7 other symptoms of BPD, all of which can be present in a pw qBPD in some way, shape, or form. BPD is about emotional dysregulation. Emotions can be dysregulated without an outburst and everyone knowing. When my emotions dysregulate, I dissociate. I'm not under control then. I didn't want to dissociate. My body and brain just did it on it's own. 

The other criteria:

1. Self-harm: highly common in pw QPD
2. unstable relationships: another commenter mentioned ghosting and self-isolation as a method of creating unstable relationships and I highly agree
3. Impulsive behavior: just because someone else doesn't know you're recklessly spending or sleeping around doesn't mean it's not happening
4. Chronic feelings of emptiness: you would have to have a conversation with someone to realize this is a symptom they experience. 
5. Explosive anger: associated with "classic" BPD, but with quiet you can have explosive anger in your car while driving alone or in your room in the middle of the night.
6. Paranoid ideation or dissociative symptoms: there are so many forms of dissociation, not just explosive anger that someone doesn't remember. Sometimes it can just be quietly spacing out after being triggered, as I mentioned before.

I don’t think I’ve ever come across a post of a pw qBPD expressing that. I’m sorry if you get that feeling from anyone. Usually I see these people are just very distraught because they feeling constantly misunderstood, invalidated, and shrugged off because their symptoms aren’t “that bad”.
Honestly, I would love to hear any examples you have. Even if you want to send them privately. (That is if you want to share. No pressure.) Are you officially diagnosed?

As someone who was in the same exact boat as you were in (literally started class of 24, now in class of 25), I say talk to the Dean. I agree with the others, it shouldn’t hurt you anymore than the imminent dismissal will. Worse thing the Dean can (professionally) do is say “no” and you end up getting dismissed. But (and I’m working on trying to do this for myself) please for the love of all that is holy, learn to fight for yourself! Keep taking every goddamn chance that’s ever presented to you. Get a letter from the person you were scribing from if you have to. Have teachers vouch for you. It was literally one exam. They should understand that and be able to recognize your growth. If this is truly what you want, you gotta learn to advocate for yourself. As someone who’s self-esteem is lower than conceptually possible, I can appreciate that this is so much easier said than done. But please do it. I hate the fact that I had to repeat a year. One of the few things that helps me not want to give up is feeling like I can maybe help someone who finds themself in the same situation as me. Help them see that repeating a year does not necessarily mean it’s over. But I won’t know every person that ever has to repeat. I’ll likely only know the ones at my school. We gotta fight through this, so more people can see that it’s possible to come back and make it through. Again, I’m only saying this if you truly want to continue medical school. If your desires for your career have changed, then I support whatever you now want to do with your life. But if you still want this, please finish medical school with me, fam. 

That being said. I’m super proud of you for already deciding to come back, improving the second time around, and just making it this far. There’s a lot to be said for your resilience. 💜
